Short map of the **business** side of LAE. Firm lists stay on [Companies & sectors](landscape.qmd); weekly tools and takeaways stay on [Lectures](lectures.qmd) and [Readings](readings.qmd). Definitions: [Glossary](glossary.qmd).

## How value is created

LAE is a **system**, not only aircraft: craft, take-off/landing sites, digital traffic and coordination, operators, customers, and supporting services ([Lectures · Week 1](lectures.qmd#week-1)).

A service creates value when it **saves time**, **cuts cost or risk**, **improves access**, or **enables a mission** other modes cannot do well. Commercial viability still hangs on willingness to pay, demand, utilization, load factor, operating cost, and investment cost — technology helps only when it improves the **economics of the full service** ([Lectures · Week 1](lectures.qmd#week-1); [Lectures · Week 3](lectures.qmd#week-3)).

Unit-cost language in class includes [CASK](glossary.qmd#business-and-economics) (passenger capacity offered) and mission-based measures for cargo or public-service work ([Lectures · Week 3](lectures.qmd#week-3); [Glossary](glossary.qmd#business-and-economics)).

## Money flow (high level)

Roles and payment directions only — **not** market sizes, deal values, or named firms. Trial programmes help teams test under controlled conditions; they are not the same as everyday commercial approval ([Lectures · Week 7](lectures.qmd#week-7)).

## Who pays whom (same roles, in words)

- **Customers / mission sponsors** pay operators for missions ([Lectures · Week 3](lectures.qmd#week-3)).
- **Operators** pay (or contract for) aircraft and maintenance, site/slot access, enabling tech and traffic services, insurance, and training — see sector roles below and [Companies & sectors](landscape.qmd).
- **Infrastructure and platform providers** earn from access, capacity, or coordination; scarce sites and route density shape competition ([Lectures · Week 2](lectures.qmd#week-2); [Lectures · Week 5](lectures.qmd#week-5)).
- **Insurers and financiers** price risk and capital ([Lectures · Week 6](lectures.qmd#week-6); [Lectures · Week 12](lectures.qmd#week-12)).
- **Public bodies** may fund trials, shared infrastructure, or public-service missions — a PPP is about value for money and risk allocation, not a free subsidy ([Lectures · Week 6](lectures.qmd#week-6)).

## How sectors fit

[Companies & sectors](landscape.qmd) groups checked entries into eleven roles:

| Role on that page | What it usually contributes |
|-------------------|-----------------------------|
| Aircraft and airframe makers | Vehicles and platforms |
| Delivery and logistics | Cargo / last-mile style missions |
| Inspection and surveying | Asset and site inspection missions |
| Emergency and medical | Public-safety / medical transport trials |
| Tourism and entertainment | Visitor / show / attraction flights |
| eVTOL and passenger trials | Passenger-oriented trial activity |
| Infrastructure and vertiports | Sites, docking, planned logistics clusters |
| Enabling technology | UTM, connectivity, shared platforms |
| Insurance and finance | Risk transfer and capital products |
| Tangible services | Hands-on flight / MRO / patrol services |
| Intangible services | Training, research, software-heavy services |

Use the map and sector lists on [Companies & sectors](landscape.qmd) for who appears where — this page does not repeat firm names.
